chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Shah narrated to us, saying: Abu Hamid narrated to us, saying: Abu Yazid Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Khalidi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Salih al-Tamimi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Hatam al-Qattan, from Hammad ibn Amr, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Do not beg with your person (self), and if something comes to you, accept it. Then he (peace be upon him) said to his companions: Shall I inform you of the worst of you? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: Those who walk about with gossip, those who separate friends, those who seek fault in the good.

key_terms.النَّمِيمَة: Gossip / Telling tales to cause discord

ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics of the worst people according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, the Prophet (peace be upon him) warns Abu Dharr against the spiritual degradation of begging, contrasting it with the dignity of contentment, while highlighting the unique honor of having companions from Iraq prepare his body for burial. He subsequently identifies the 'worst of people' as those who spread *namima* (gossip), create discord among friends, and seek faults in the righteous, a triad of vices that destroys social cohesion. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on inner purity and social harmony, linking personal conduct to communal stability.
